scope: Propagate API request disconnects into native PDF/DOCX parser child work, kill and reap cancelled children, and enforce bounded streaming parser output on Windows and Linux.

evidence.summary: 36 tests passed, including actual sleeping and overproducing child-process cases, route-level disconnect propagation, profile ownership/review boundaries, native parsing, and regressions. ResourceWarnings are treated as errors.

The real Chromium profile import, extraction review, save/reload, named resume history, failed OCR warning and no-profile-mutation journey passed. Disconnect cancellation itself is asserted at the API route integration boundary, not by a browser abort test.
683 tests ran; zero failures/errors; one optional PostgreSQL test skipped because MJOBS_TEST_POSTGRES_URL was unset.

requirement_limitations: Cancellation is wired through native PDF/DOCX parser child execution. OCR already in progress is not immediately interrupted on client disconnect; it retains its independent bounded tool and total deadlines.

Browser abort behavior was not separately driven through Chromium; endpoint disconnect semantics and actual child termination are covered by API integration and real subprocess tests, while the existing Chromium profile import/review journey passed.
